report.md:
## This week

You posted 3 videos this week. That is way down from last week's 10. Views dropped too, you went from about 3,700 views per video down to about 1,350. Your best one this week was "The real reason I said yes...", which pulled 1,433 views. Your weakest was "even though I made six figures last month I still took three trains in a bus", at 830 views. Heads up though, both of these are only 1 day old, so these numbers could still climb. All three videos this week were talking to camera, so you did not really test any other style.

## Is it how you film, or what you say?

Right now, what you say matters more than how you film it. Looking across all your videos, the topic and the way you structure the video explain a lot more of the difference in views than the camera style does. Talking to camera versus voice over footage barely moves the needle on its own. The honest truth is you have not run a clean test yet, like filming the exact same script two different ways, so this is your best guess, not a sure thing. You do film certain topics in certain styles a lot, so it is a little hard to fully separate the two. One thing worth watching: your come-up videos filmed as voice over footage hit way bigger numbers than the same topic filmed talking to camera. That is one combo worth testing on purpose. Bottom line right now: what you talk about is driving views more than how you shoot it, but you have not truly put that to the test yet.

## What is working

Your how you got started videos usually get about twice your normal views. You have posted 27 of these, so that is a real pattern. Videos with a link in bio call to action do huge numbers, almost 15 times your usual views, and you have tried this 8 times. Videos told as a full story, not just a moment, also do great, over 5 times your normal views, across 8 videos.

## Try this next week

Film a how you got started video as voice over footage instead of talking to camera, to test if that combo is really the magic. Tell one video as a full story with a beginning, middle, and end, and add a link in bio at the end. Try a longer video, over 60 seconds, since your longer ones have been massively outperforming your short ones.

best.md:
This video did badly. It only got 2,853 views, well under what a normal video of yours gets, and way under what your "how you got started" videos usually pull in.

Your opening line was "from a girl that booked $10K in her first 48 hours." That is a strong hook on paper, it promises a clear payoff. But there is no speech in this video, so it looks like the words on screen had to do all the work with no voice backing them up, and that likely hurt your scroll-stopping power in the first 3 seconds.

There is no transcript to check if you kept giving people reasons to stay after the opening, which makes it hard to know if the middle of the video held attention.

There was no call to action tagged on this one. Next time, ask for a follow after you deliver the $10K story, not at the very end when people have already scrolled off.

One thing to try next time: add your voice talking through the story, don't just rely on text or caption. Your "how you got started" videos do over two times what your other videos do, so lean into that bucket again, but make sure your voice carries the hook this time.

worst.md:
This one did badly. It only got 339 views, while your normal video gets way more, about 4,651. That is a huge drop, not a small dip.

Your opening line was "one thing abt me...i'm gonna hit my 10K steps even if it means walking in circles around the airport." It is relatable, but it does not stop the scroll fast. It takes too long to get to the funny or interesting part, so people swipe before they find out why it matters.

The video is only 6 seconds long with no speech, just a clip and music. That means there was nothing pulling people to keep watching after the first moment. Nothing new got revealed, no twist, no payoff.

There was no call to action at all. You could have asked people to comment their own weird step habit, or asked them to follow for more real life moments like this.

Next time, try starting with the funniest or most surprising part first, like the walking in circles part, instead of saving it for later.
